intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus or shared shuttle to Reykjavik BSÍ terminal. Rest briefly at a café near the bus terminal and grab a warm drink to recover from the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the long drive north toward Siglufjörður (approximately 4.5–5 hours via Route 1 and Route 76). Stop at the town of Akureyri briefly to stretch, grab groceries at Bónus supermarket (Iceland's most budget-friendly chain) for snacks and supplies for the week. Continue north along the scenic Tröllaskagi Peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by late afternoon or early evening. Check in, unpack, and settle in. Take a short stroll around the charming harbor town to get oriented. Keep an eye out for the northern lights after dark — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it excellent for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at a café near Reykjavik BSÍ bus terminal (budget ~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks and groceries purchased at Bónus supermarket in Akureyri (budget ~1,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal at the hotel using groceries from Bónus — simple pasta or soup to recover from travel (budget ~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is strongly recommended for this itinerary. Book in advance for the best budget rates. Drive carefully on Route 76 as winter roads can be icy and narrow through the Tröllaskagi Peninsula tunnels. Check road conditions at road.is before driving. Dress in warm layers upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Siglufjörður on foot. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's best regional museums, showcasing the town's herring fishing boom era. Entry is modest and well worth it for the historical insight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south along Route 76 to explore the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Stop at the small village of Hofsós, which has a stunning geothermal infinity pool (Hofsós Swimming Pool) overlooking Skagafjörður fjord — one of Iceland's most scenic and least-crowded public pools. Entry is very affordable (~900 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Head up to a hillside viewpoint above the town for northern lights watching. The steep mountains surrounding the fjord create a dramatic backdrop for aurora displays. Bring a thermos of hot cocoa.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or eggs at the hotel (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich from hotel supplies and eat at Hofsós by the pool (budget ~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Ársæll restaurant or Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — try the fish soup, a hearty and budget-friendly local staple (budget ~2,500–3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is one of Iceland's hidden gems and rarely crowded in January. Bring a towel and swimsuit. Check aurora forecast at en.vedur.is — a KP index of 3 or above with clear skies is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (free) to the neighboring ghost fjord of Héðinsfjörður — an abandoned and hauntingly beautiful valley. Walk along the shoreline of this uninhabited fjord surrounded by snow-dusted mountains. A truly off-the-beaten-path experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður and hike up toward the old ski lifts above town (Skíðasvæðið). Even without skiing, the walk offers sweeping panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding peaks. In January the daylight is limited (roughly 5–6 hours), so make the most of the midday light.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Siglufjörður municipal swimming pool and hot tubs (sundlaug) — a beloved local tradition and one of the most affordable ways to warm up and socialize in Iceland (~1,000 ISK). Afterward, northern lights watch from the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — yogurt, skyr, and fruit (budget ~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch to Héðinsfjörður — thermos of soup and bread (budget ~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — grilled lamb chops or fish fillets from Bónus (budget ~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Héðinsfjörður is accessible only via tunnel — no toll. Wear waterproof hiking boots as the valley floor can be muddy or icy. Daylight in January in Siglufjörður is roughly 9:30am–3:30pm, so plan outdoor activities accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Akureyri (about 1 hour via Route 82 and Route 1). Explore Iceland's second-largest city on foot. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched above the town — free entry and beautiful views. Stroll the pedestrian shopping street Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — free entry and a peaceful winter walk. Then head to the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for a warm, affordable cultural stop (~1,000 ISK entry). Browse the Bónus or Krónan supermarket for restocking supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Soak at Sundlaug Akureyrar — the city's large geothermal swimming complex with multiple hot tubs and pools, very affordable (~1,100 ISK). Drive back to Siglufjörður or, if tired, consider staying overnight in Akureyri at a budget guesthouse to save driving.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu or a bakery in Akureyri — try a bowl of lamb soup (kjötsúpa) at a local café (budget ~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri has a budget lunch/dinner menu, or grab a hot dog from N1 gas station — Iceland's iconic budget meal (budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri has heart-shaped traffic lights — a charming local detail. Stock up on groceries here as Siglufjörður has limited shopping options. The drive back to Siglufjörður via Route 82 along Eyjafjörður is scenic even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður via the Tröllaskagi tunnels to Dalvík (about 45 minutes). Take the free Hrísey island ferry (short crossing) to the small island of Hrísey in Eyjafjörður — known as the 'Pearl of Eyjafjörður.' Explore the quiet village and birdlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the mainland and drive to Árskógssandur to visit the Bjórböðin Beer Spa — a unique Icelandic experience of soaking in warm beer baths with stunning fjord views. Note: this is a splurge (~7,900 ISK per person) but can be a memorable budget exception. Alternatively, skip and soak at Dalvík's public pool for ~1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður. Northern lights watch from the harbor or hillside. The clear fjord air and dark skies make this one of the best spots in Iceland for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Hrísey island — bring supplies from hotel (budget ~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty stew at hotel using lamb and root vegetables from Bónus (budget ~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Hrísey ferry runs regularly and is free for foot passengers. The island is very quiet in January but offers a peaceful escape. Check Bjórböðin availability and book in advance if interested — it fills up even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Akureyri toward Lake Mývatn (about 1 hour from Akureyri, 2 hours from Siglufjörður via Route 1). Stop at Goðafoss waterfall en route — one of Iceland's most spectacular and easily accessible waterfalls, free to visit. The winter ice formations around the falls are stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn area: visit the Námaskarð geothermal field (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of boiling mud pools, steam vents, and sulfur deposits. Completely free and otherworldly. Then walk around the Dimmuborgir lava field, a maze of dramatic volcanic rock formations (free).
day_by_day.evening: Soak at the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a more affordable and less crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon (~5,500 ISK). The milky blue geothermal pools surrounded by volcanic landscape are magical at night, especially if the northern lights appear. Drive back toward Siglufjörður or stay locally.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Gamli Bærinn café near Mývatn — try the geothermal rye bread (hverabrauð) with smoked trout, a local specialty (budget ~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered or Vogafjós Farm Restaurant near Mývatn for a splurge on fresh local dairy and lamb (budget ~3,000–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn is a full day trip from Siglufjörður (roughly 2 hours each way). Consider an overnight stay at Mývatn to reduce driving. Budget accommodation options include Hlíð Guesthouse or camping huts (if open in January). Hverir smells strongly of sulfur — completely normal.

day_by_day.morning: If staying near Mývatn, explore Skútustaðagígar pseudo-craters at the south shore of the lake — free walking trail around these unique volcanic formations created by steam explosions. Then visit Lofthellir lava cave (book guided tour in advance, ~8,000 ISK) for a stunning underground ice cave experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive north back toward Siglufjörður via Route 1 and Route 82 along the Eyjafjörður coastline. Stop at Grenivík village for a short coastal walk with views across the fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Hotel Siglunes. Rest and warm up. Evening northern lights vigil from the hotel or harbor area. January offers some of the longest and darkest nights of the year — prime aurora season.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or guesthouse breakfast near Mývatn (budget ~1,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed supplies or gas station food on the drive back (budget ~1,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — warm up with fish of the day and local beer (budget ~3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Lofthellir lava cave tours must be pre-booked through local operators. The ice formations inside are spectacular in winter. Dress in full waterproof layers for the cave. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can be challenging — check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Walk along the harbor and watch local fishing boats. Visit the Síldarminjasafnið (Herring Era Museum) gift shop for affordable local souvenirs like dried fish and Icelandic wool items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the trail toward Hvanneyrarskúti viewpoint above Siglufjörður for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding mountains. The hike is moderate and takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip. In winter, microspikes or crampons are recommended.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the Siglufjörður hot tub and pool complex (sundlaug). Afterward, try stargazing and northern lights watching from the beach at the edge of town — one of the darkest spots in northern Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — skyr with granola and coffee (budget ~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Warm soup and bread at Kaffi Rauðka or self-catered (budget ~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner — baked cod with potatoes and butter, a classic Icelandic home meal (budget ~1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day to recharge mid-trip. Siglufjörður is a wonderful place to simply slow down and experience authentic Icelandic small-town life. The town has a population of only about 1,200 people.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along Route 76 through the Skagi Peninsula toward Sauðárkrókur (about 1.5 hours). Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagafjarðar) at Glaumbær — a preserved 18th-century turf farm and one of Iceland's best folk museums (~1,500 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Varmahlíð area and visit the Reykjafoss waterfall and the geothermal area at Reykir in Skagafjörður — a small, free natural hot spring area. Explore the scenic Skagafjörður valley, known for its horse farms and dramatic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður via Route 75 and Route 76. The evening drive through the mountains offers excellent northern lights viewing opportunities if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café at Glaumbær Heritage Museum or packed lunch (budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — lamb soup with bread, made from ingredients purchased at Sauðárkrókur's Krónan supermarket (budget ~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm is one of Iceland's most authentic historical sites. The drive through Skagafjörður is particularly scenic. Sauðárkrókur has a Krónan supermarket — good opportunity to restock supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west on Route 1 toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula direction, stopping at Hvammstangi (about 2 hours from Siglufjörður). Visit the Icelandic Seal Center (Selasetur Íslands) — a charming and affordable museum about Iceland's seal population (~1,000 ISK). Walk along the Vatnsnes Peninsula coastline to spot wild seals at Illugastaðir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Hvítserkur — a dramatic 15-meter basalt rock stack rising from the sea, resembling a dragon drinking from the ocean. Free to visit and one of Iceland's most photogenic natural landmarks. The short walk from the parking area is easy.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður (about 2 hours). The long return drive offers prime northern lights viewing from the roadside — pull over safely if the aurora appears.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at hotel (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Hvítserkur viewpoint — thermos of hot soup and sandwiches (budget ~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Ársæll or Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — treat yourself to pan-fried Arctic char (budget ~3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hvítserkur is best photographed at high tide when the rock appears to rise dramatically from the sea. The trail down to the beach can be icy in January — use caution. Seal sightings at Illugastaðir are common year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east toward Akureyri and continue to the Eyjafjörður valley. Visit Munkaþverárklaustur monastery ruins and the scenic Munkaþverá church. Explore the peaceful Eyjafjörður valley farmland dusted with winter snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laufás turf farm and church (free exterior, small fee for interior) — a beautifully preserved 19th-century turf farmhouse on the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður with stunning fjord views. Continue to Grenivík for a coastal walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic Route 82 coastal road. Stop at a dark pullout along the fjord for northern lights watching. This is one of the best nights to attempt a dedicated aurora hunt — bring a camera on a tripod for long-exposure shots.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the Eyjafjörður valley (budget ~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered celebratory dinner at hotel — skyr cheesecake for dessert, a classic Icelandic treat (budget ~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Laufás is one of Iceland's best-preserved turf farms. The Eyjafjörður valley is the longest fjord in Iceland and offers stunning winter scenery. Aurora forecast apps like 'My Aurora Forecast' are useful for planning evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Siglufjörður. Take a slow morning walk around the entire harbor and old fishing village district. Visit the local church (Siglufjörðarkirkja) — free and architecturally charming. Browse any local craft shops for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Hofsós geothermal infinity pool for a final relaxing soak with fjord views — the perfect way to spend a last afternoon in northern Iceland. Stop at Hofsós village viewpoint for panoramic photos of Skagafjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights watch from Siglufjörður. Pack bags for early departure the next day. Enjoy a farewell dinner in town. Reflect on the trip over a warm Icelandic coffee and kleinur (Icelandic doughnuts).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — use up remaining supplies (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Hofsós (budget ~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Splurge farewell dinner at Kaffi Rauðka — fish of the day with Icelandic craft beer (budget ~3,500–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Pack and prepare the night before for an early morning departure. Settle any hotel bills. Download offline maps for the return drive to Reykjavik/Keflavik. Check road conditions for the following morning at road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Siglufjörður. Drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 4.5–5 hours). Stop at Blönduós for fuel and a coffee. Continue south on Route 1 through the dramatic Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau — stunning winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik with time to spare. Drop off rental car at Keflavik Airport or Reykjavik location. If time allows, take a final walk along Reykjavik's Sæbraut coastal path or visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free exterior, small fee for tower). Head to Keflavik Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Check in for return flight at Keflavik International Airport. Grab a final Icelandic hot dog at the airport or a bowl of skyr before departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, and raw Icelandic nature.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure — finish any remaining food supplies (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Gas station or roadside café stop in Blönduós or Borgarnes (budget ~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport food or final hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu in Reykjavik (budget ~1,000–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for airport check-in and security. The drive from Siglufjörður to Keflavik Airport is approximately 5–5.5 hours — plan accordingly. Return rental car with a full tank of fuel to avoid extra charges. Keflavik duty-free is one of the best places to buy Icelandic spirits and chocolate at competitive prices.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up a pre-booked rental car (4WD essential for January conditions). Grab a coffee and light breakfast at the airport café before beginning the long scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður (~5.5 hours via Route 1 and Tunnel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north through Akureyri area, stopping briefly at Goðafoss Waterfall (Waterfall of the Gods) en route — a stunning frozen-edged cascade even in winter. Stretch your legs and take photos before continuing the final stretch to Siglufjörður through the Héðinsfjörður tunnels.
day_by_day.evening: Check into Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður. Freshen up, unpack, and take a short stroll through the charming, quiet fishing town to get oriented. The town is beautifully lit in winter. Head to bed early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Airport café at Keflavik — grab a coffee and a skyr yogurt or pastry (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from an airport kiosk or stop at a petrol station N1 or Orkan along Route 1 for a hot dog (pylsur) — Iceland's iconic budget snack (~500–800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Restaurant at Hotel Siglunes or Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — cozy local spot serving Icelandic fish soup and lamb dishes (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January roads in Iceland can be icy and treacherous. Check road conditions at road.is before departing the airport. The drive is approximately 450 km — allow 5.5–6.5 hours with stops. Arrive before dark (sunset around 15:30 in January). Book rental car 4WD in advance.

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, explore Siglufjörður on foot. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's best regional museums, documenting the town's rich herring fishing history. Fascinating even in winter (~1,800 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the short scenic coastal road around the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Stop at Hofsós village (~45 min south) to see the stunning infinity-edge geothermal swimming pool perched above the fjord — one of Iceland's most scenic pools. Swim and soak with fjord views (~1,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. After dinner, bundle up and head to a dark spot just outside town (minimal light pollution here) to watch for the Northern Lights. January offers up to 17 hours of darkness — excellent aurora viewing odds on clear nights. Check aurora forecast at en.vedur.is.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet (if included) or Café Bláa Kannan nearby — eggs, skyr, fresh bread (~2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hofsós — bring packed sandwiches or stop at a small local café
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — hearty lamb soup or pan-fried Arctic char with Icelandic bread (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is one of Iceland's hidden gems and rarely crowded in winter. Bring a swimsuit and towel. Aurora activity: check cloud cover forecast — Siglufjörður's fjord location can trap clouds but also offers shelter. Dress in full thermal layers for evening aurora watching.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along the scenic Route 76 toward Akureyri (~1.5 hours), Iceland's 'Capital of the North.' Explore the charming town center, visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, and browse the small but lively pedestrian shopping street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, magical in winter snow. Then head to the nearby Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a beloved local geothermal pool complex with hot tubs and steam rooms (~1,000 ISK). A true local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before the drive back to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, stay in Akureyri if weather looks promising for northern lights viewing from the open valley — then return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siglufjörður
meals.lunch: Bautinn Restaurant in Akureyri — classic Icelandic comfort food, lamb soup and fish of the day, great value (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Rub23 in Akureyri — popular mid-range restaurant with excellent sushi and grilled fish (~4,000–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a great day-trip base. Road conditions on Route 76 can be icy — drive carefully. Akureyri has good supermarkets (Krónan, Bónus) to stock up on snacks and supplies for the week. January daylight is only about 5–6 hours so plan outdoor activities between 11:00–15:30.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure east toward Lake Mývatn (~1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Akureyri). This otherworldly volcanic landscape is one of Iceland's most dramatic. Begin with a walk around the Dimmuborgir lava formations — bizarre black lava pillars and arches, like a frozen alien city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — the 'Blue Lagoon of the North' but far less crowded and equally spectacular. Milky-blue geothermal water rich in minerals at ~36–40°C. Spend 1.5–2 hours here (~5,500 ISK). Afterward, visit the Hverfjall volcanic crater rim for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður as darkness falls. Stop along the roadside if the Northern Lights appear — the open landscapes around Mývatn offer spectacular aurora viewing with reflections on the lake. Return to hotel by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Café Við Mývatn near the nature baths — Icelandic lamb stew and freshly baked bread (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant or Kaffi Rauðka upon return (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths must be booked in advance in winter. Bring swimsuit and towel. The drive around Mývatn can be icy — 4WD essential. Hverfjall crater walk may be closed or difficult in heavy snow — check locally. This is one of the best aurora-watching regions in Iceland due to low light pollution.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning in Siglufjörður. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and take a peaceful winter walk along the harbor waterfront. The town is beautifully quiet and photogenic in winter light. Visit the small local shops and pick up Icelandic woolens (lopapeysa sweaters) at the craft store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the nearby Skagafjörður valley (~45 min south) — known as Iceland's horse capital. Visit a local horse farm for a short Icelandic horse experience or guided winter ride through snowy landscapes. Icelandic horses are famously friendly and sturdy. (~6,000–8,000 ISK for a guided ride).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a local guide who monitors aurora forecasts and drives to optimal dark-sky viewing spots around the fjords. Guides maximize your chances of seeing the aurora borealis dancing overhead. (~8,000–12,000 ISK).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a local bakery in Sauðárkrókur town in Skagafjörður — soup and fresh bread (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka — try the pan-fried catfish or lamb fillet with Icelandic potatoes (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book the horse riding experience in advance — winter availability is limited but the experience is magical in snow. The Northern Lights tour is weather-dependent; reputable operators will reschedule if cloud cover prevents viewing. Dress in maximum thermal layers for the evening tour.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east toward the Eastfjords region, beginning the long scenic journey south along the Ring Road (Route 1). First stop: the dramatic Goðafoss waterfall for a proper visit with time to walk the viewing paths along both banks (~1.5 hours from Siglufjörður).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to the geothermal valley of Haukadalur to visit Geysir and Strokkur geyser — Strokkur erupts every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Walk the geothermal field boardwalks and marvel at the bubbling hot springs and fumaroles. (~2.5 hours from Goðafoss).
day_by_day.evening: Check into accommodation near Geysir/Gullfoss area (book a guesthouse in Flúðir or Selfoss for the night — mid-range guesthouse ~15,000–20,000 ISK). Alternatively, visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir this evening — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated outdoor pool surrounded by bubbling geothermal springs and small geysers (~3,200 ISK).

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before checkout
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café — lamb soup or fish and chips (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Minniborgir Restaurant near Geysir or dinner at guesthouse in Flúðir — hearty Icelandic lamb and root vegetable dishes (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~4–5 hours total). Check road.is before departure. This day transitions from the north to the south of Iceland. Pack all belongings from Hotel Siglunes. The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is far less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon and extremely atmospheric in winter — steam rising from the pool into the cold night air.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gullfoss Waterfall — the 'Golden Falls,' one of Iceland's most iconic waterfalls. In January, the falls are partially frozen with dramatic ice formations. Walk to the multiple viewpoints. Then complete the famous Golden Circle by visiting Þingvellir National Park — where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament was held.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir — the crystal-clear glacial water between the tectonic plates offers visibility up to 100 meters. Snorkeling tours include dry suits (~25,000–35,000 ISK). This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience — floating between two continents in some of the clearest water on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Reykjavik (~45 min from Þingvellir). Check into a mid-range hotel or guesthouse in Reykjavik (~18,000–25,000 ISK/night). Explore the lively Laugavegur street, visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church exterior, and enjoy the city atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast near Flúðir
meals.lunch: Þingvellir visitor center café — Icelandic fish soup and rye bread (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavik — famous for cast-iron pan-fried fish, excellent mid-range seafood (~4,500–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires booking well in advance — January is cold but the dry suit keeps you warm. Minimum age/health requirements apply. Water temperature is ~2°C year-round. Þingvellir is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — allow 1.5–2 hours to explore. Reykjavik hotel: consider Guesthouse Óðinn or similar mid-range option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (~50 min from Reykjavik, near Keflavik). Book the Comfort package — includes entrance, silica mud mask, algae mask, and a drink. Soak in the world-famous milky-blue 37–39°C mineral-rich waters. Arrive early (first slot) to avoid crowds (~12,000–16,000 ISK for Comfort package).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik. Explore the city's cultural highlights: visit the Harpa Concert Hall (free to enter the lobby — stunning geometric glass architecture), walk the colorful old harbor area, and browse the Kolaportið flea market (open Saturdays) for Icelandic snacks, wool goods, and vintage items.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavik's vibrant restaurant scene. After dinner, join a Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from Reykjavik — guides drive to dark countryside locations away from city light pollution to maximize aurora viewing chances (~8,000–12,000 ISK). Tours typically run 21:00–00:00.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik hotel breakfast or Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur — exceptional sourdough, pastries, and coffee (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon café (light snacks included in some packages) or bring packed lunch
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — mid-range Icelandic grill restaurant with locally sourced lamb, fish, and wild game (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be booked weeks in advance — it sells out completely, especially weekends. Bring flip-flops for walking between changing rooms and pool. Remove all jewelry before entering (minerals discolor metal). Northern Lights tour: reputable operators include Arctic Adventures and Reykjavik Excursions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast from Reykjavik eastward. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — unique in that you can walk behind the curtain of water (may be icy/closed in January — check). Then Skógafoss Waterfall — a powerful 60-meter cascade with a rainbow in the mist. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt column formations, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Walk carefully — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous. Then visit Dyrhólaey arch promontory for coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse near Vík or Kirkjubæjarklaustur (~15,000–20,000 ISK). The remote south coast offers exceptional Northern Lights viewing — minimal light pollution and wide open skies. Set an aurora alarm app and step outside if skies clear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik before departure
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík — great fish and chips with black sand beach views (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner or Ströndin Bistro in Vík — Icelandic lamb and fish dishes in a cozy setting (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is one of Iceland's most dangerous — NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Sneaker waves have claimed lives. Stay well back from the water. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the falls is often iced over in January — check with locals before attempting. Pack crampons/microspikes for icy paths.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Skaftafell in Vatnajökull National Park (~1.5 hours east of Vík). Meet your guide for the Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull — strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified guide. Explore stunning blue ice formations, crevasses, and ice caves. (~15,000–20,000 ISK for a 3-hour guided hike).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike, drive to the famous Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — a breathtaking lake filled with floating blue icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. Walk the shore and watch seals. Then visit Diamond Beach — where ice chunks wash up on black sand, glittering like diamonds. Extraordinary in the low winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Return west toward Vík or Kirkjubæjarklaustur area for overnight. The open landscape between Jökulsárlón and Vík is prime Northern Lights territory — watch for aurora on the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast near Vík
meals.lunch: Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon café — lamb soup and sandwiches (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Return to guesthouse dinner or Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — home-cooked Icelandic meals in a charming village café (~3,000–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hike MUST be booked in advance — only go with a certified guide, never attempt independently. Wear warm, waterproof layers and sturdy boots (crampons provided). Jökulsárlón is most dramatic in late afternoon when the low golden light reflects on the icebergs. January temperatures here can drop to -10°C with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the drive back westward along the South Coast, stopping at the Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon near Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a stunning 100-meter deep, 2 km long canyon carved by glacial water. Walk the canyon rim trail for dramatic views (trail may be partially icy — use microspikes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur (~2 hours west) — Iceland's premier volcano and earthquake exhibition. Highly interactive and educational, giving context to all the geological wonders you've witnessed. (~2,500 ISK entry). Continue to the Þórsmörk valley area viewpoint if road conditions allow.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Reykjavik. Check back into your Reykjavik hotel. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the city — explore the nightlife on Laugavegur, visit a cozy bar, or attend a live music event at Harpa or a local venue. Reykjavik has a surprisingly vibrant music scene.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lava Centre café in Hvolsvöllur — fish soup and Icelandic rye bread (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbor — legendary lobster soup and grilled fish skewers, excellent value (~2,500–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon may have limited access in January due to snow and ice — check locally. The Lava Centre is excellent for families and anyone wanting to understand Iceland's volcanic geology. Reykjavik hotel: rebook your earlier accommodation or try a different property for variety.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik's cultural highlights in depth. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — comprehensive collection covering 1,200 years of Icelandic history and culture (~2,000 ISK). Then walk to Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city views (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum — a futuristic glass dome building with Iceland's only indoor ice cave, northern lights planetarium show, and nature of Iceland exhibitions (~3,500–5,000 ISK). Excellent for experiencing Iceland's natural phenomena in an immersive setting. Afterward, relax at Sundhöll Reykjavíkur — the city's oldest geothermal swimming pool, a beautiful 1930s Art Deco building (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — either join another guided tour or drive independently to the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir for dark skies. Alternatively, enjoy a special farewell dinner in Reykjavik at a nicer restaurant as a trip highlight.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik Roasters café — specialty coffee and pastries, a local favorite (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café Loki opposite Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (rúgbrauð with smoked lamb, herring, and skyr) (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Fishmarket Restaurant (Fiskmarkaðurinn) — upscale Icelandic seafood with Asian influences, splurge-worthy farewell dinner (~7,000–10,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Perlan's northern lights show is a great backup if you haven't seen the real aurora yet. Sundhöll pool is a beloved local institution — very authentic compared to tourist-oriented spas. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance. January evenings in Reykjavik: aurora forecasts can change rapidly — keep the app open.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last-minute souvenir shopping on Laugavegur street. Pick up Icelandic chocolates (Nói Síríus), skyr, lopapeysa wool sweaters, or lava salt as gifts. Visit the Kolaportið flea market if open. Return the rental car to the Reykjavik drop-off point or drive to Keflavik Airport (~45 min).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik Airport with plenty of time (recommended 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights). Browse the duty-free shops — Iceland's airport duty-free has excellent Icelandic spirits (Brennivín aquavit, Icelandic vodka), chocolate, and skincare products. Grab a final Icelandic hot dog at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of glaciers, geothermal pools, northern lights, and one of the world's most dramatic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik hotel breakfast — enjoy a full Icelandic spread of smoked salmon, skyr, flatbread, and eggs
meals.lunch: Airport café or duty-free food court — Icelandic lamb sandwich or soup (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank of fuel — petrol stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. Allow extra time in January for possible icy road conditions to the airport. Keflavik Airport has good duty-free but prices are lower before security for Icelandic souvenirs. Keep one layer of warm clothes accessible in carry-on for the walk between terminal and aircraft.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs, collect luggage, and meet private transfer driver. Enjoy a scenic 5-hour luxury private transfer northward toward Siglufjörður, stopping at Borgarnes for a brief stretch. Marvel at the dramatic lava fields and snow-dusted mountains along Route 1 and Route 76.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður early afternoon. Check in and settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord. Take a gentle, self-guided walk along the snow-lined harbor front of this charming herring-era fishing village. Visit the iconic red warehouses and admire the steep mountains encircling the town.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from the overnight flight. Step outside after dark for a first attempt at spotting the Northern Lights directly from the hotel's waterfront — Siglufjörður's minimal light pollution makes it an excellent natural vantage point. Bundle up and scan the sky from the harbor pier.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments provided during private airport transfer (pre-arranged charcuterie and coffee box)
meals.lunch: Á Bakkanum restaurant in Siglufjörður — cozy local bistro with fresh fish soup and Icelandic lamb sandwiches
meals.dinner: Hótel Siglunes dining room — enjoy a curated welcome dinner of pan-seared Arctic char with root vegetable purée and Icelandic craft beer or local spirits

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance (approx. 5 hours drive). Pack aurora-watching layers for the evening. January sunset is around 16:30, so darkness sets in early — ideal for aurora spotting. Rest is essential after the overnight flight.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely hotel breakfast, embark on a guided snowshoe hike up the lower slopes of the mountains surrounding Siglufjörður. A local guide will lead you through pristine snow fields with panoramic views of the frozen fjord below. The crisp Arctic air and untouched winter landscape make this an extraordinary premium nature experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, spread across restored fjord-side warehouses. Explore interactive exhibits on the 20th-century herring boom that shaped this town. Afterward, warm up at the hotel's lounge with Icelandic hot chocolate and skyr parfait.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a small-group guided aurora tour departing from Siglufjörður into the surrounding countryside. Your expert guide will use aurora forecast apps and drive to optimal dark-sky vantage points in the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Bring a tripod for photography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet — smoked salmon, skyr, fresh bread, Icelandic cheeses, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box from hotel (smoked lamb flatbread, fruit, thermos of soup) enjoyed with mountain views
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — intimate local restaurant serving Icelandic lamb stew and fresh catch of the day with Icelandic wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe rental can be arranged through the hotel. Aurora tour should be booked in advance through a local Siglufjörður operator. Aurora forecast for January in northern Iceland is excellent — this region sits near the auroral oval.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the spectacular Héðinsfjörður mountain pass (weather permitting) or take the tunnel to neighboring Ólafsfjörður for a scenic coastal walk. Explore the quiet village and its colorful houses reflected in the still fjord waters. Return to Siglufjörður via the Strákagil valley overlook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a private in-hotel spa treatment session — arrange a traditional Icelandic hot stone massage or deep tissue treatment through the hotel's concierge service. Spend the remainder of the afternoon reading by the fire in the hotel lounge with panoramic fjord views.
day_by_day.evening: Private Northern Lights photography session — hire a local professional aurora photographer to guide you to the best compositions around the fjord, using the town's colorful reflections on the water as foreground. This is a premium, intimate experience unique to Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, freshly squeezed juice, and Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Segull 67 Brewery in Siglufjörður — Iceland's northernmost craft brewery, serving artisan pizzas and locally brewed ales with fjord views
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner experience arranged through Hotel Siglunes — four-course tasting menu featuring reindeer tenderloin, langoustine bisque, and Skyr mousse with crowberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions before driving the mountain pass — Route 82 can be closed in severe winter weather. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel is a reliable alternative. Book the private aurora photographer at least 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður for a full-day scenic drive south toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 3.5 hours). Stop at Varmahlíð for a coffee break, then continue through the dramatic Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau, covered in snow and ice in January. Arrive at Snæfellsnes by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk the Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach, see the dramatic Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks, and visit the mystical Arnarstapi lava arch coastline. The moody winter light creates extraordinary photographic conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at Hotel Búðir — one of Iceland's most romantic and remote luxury properties, set beside a historic black church on a lava field with Snæfellsjökull as backdrop. Dine in the hotel's acclaimed restaurant. Watch for Northern Lights from the hotel's isolated position, far from any light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes final breakfast — stocked thermos of coffee and pastries for the road
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar — legendary cliffside café serving homemade soup, bread, and cakes with ocean views
meals.dinner: Hotel Búðir restaurant — celebrated fine dining featuring locally foraged ingredients, Icelandic lamb, and fresh Atlantic seafood with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel/transition day. Confirm Hotel Búðir reservation well in advance — it is one of Iceland's most sought-after luxury stays. Snæfellsnes roads are generally well-maintained but drive carefully on icy sections.

day_by_day.morning: Guided glacier walk on Snæfellsjökull glacier with a certified local guide — strap on crampons and explore the ice cap of this iconic volcano. The guides provide all safety equipment and share geological and folkloric stories about the glacier. Views of the surrounding peninsula and ocean are breathtaking on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vatnshellir lava tube cave — a 8,000-year-old lava tunnel beneath the Snæfellsnes lava field. A guided tour descends into the dramatic underground chambers with helmet and torch. Afterward, explore the charming village of Grundarfjörður and photograph the iconic Kirkjufell mountain, Iceland's most photographed peak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Búðir. Enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail at the hotel bar — try an Icelandic Arctic Thyme gin and tonic. Northern Lights vigil from the hotel terrace after dinner. The isolated location and dark skies make this one of Iceland's finest aurora viewing spots.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Búðir breakfast — continental spread with Icelandic specialties, fresh skyr, and hot porridge
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch from Hotel Búðir (smoked lamb wraps, fruit, hot soup in thermos) on the glacier or at Kirkjufell viewpoint
meals.dinner: Hotel Búðir restaurant — second evening, try the catch-of-the-day with Icelandic herb butter and local vegetable sides, paired with Burgundy white wine

day_by_day.notes: Glacier walk requires booking in advance through Snæfellsjökull guides (e.g., Snjófell or Summit Adventure Guides). Minimum physical fitness required. Dress in warm, waterproof layers — the glacier can be extremely cold and windy in January.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hotel Búðir and drive the northern Snæfellsnes coastal road through Stykkishólmur — a charming town with colorful houses and a distinctive lighthouse. Visit the Norwegian House museum and browse the small harbor. Continue east toward Reykjavik (approximately 2 hours from Stykkishólmur).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in at a luxury Reykjavik hotel (e.g., The Retreat at Blue Lagoon or ION Adventure Hotel — pre-booked). Freshen up and then visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church for panoramic city views from the tower. Explore the Laugavegur shopping street for premium Icelandic wool goods, design items, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants followed by a Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from Reykjavik — a guided minibus tour takes you to dark-sky locations outside the city to maximize aurora viewing chances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Búðir farewell breakfast
meals.lunch: Narfeyrarstofa restaurant in Stykkishólmur — beloved local institution serving langoustine soup, pan-fried fish, and homemade cakes
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a New Nordic tasting menu with foraged and fermented Icelandic ingredients (reservation essential, book weeks in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Dill Restaurant reservations must be made well in advance. The Northern Lights tour from Reykjavik typically departs around 21:00 and returns by midnight. Bring camera with manual settings for aurora photography.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience — book the premium 'Retreat Spa' package at the Blue Lagoon, which includes private changing facilities, in-water floating massage, silica mud mask, algae mask, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon (less crowded than the main lagoon). The milky-blue waters at 38-40°C are extraordinary in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Blue Lagoon — enjoy the in-water bar, lava restaurant lunch, and steam caves. The dramatic winter landscape of snow-dusted lava fields surrounding the lagoon creates a surreal, otherworldly atmosphere. Depart mid-afternoon and return to Reykjavik.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant Friday evening scene. Visit the Kolaportið flea market if open, or browse the old harbor area. Enjoy cocktails at the Sky Bar at Canopy by Hilton for panoramic city views, then dinner at a top Reykjavik restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast in Reykjavik — full Icelandic spread
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — premium dining with views over the geothermal lagoon; try the langoustine and Icelandic lamb dishes
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — rooftop fine dining with panoramic Reykjavik views, serving dry-aged Icelandic beef and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa tickets sell out months in advance — book immediately upon trip confirmation. Arrive at the Blue Lagoon early (first slot recommended). Remove all jewelry before entering the water as the silica and minerals can damage metals.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle private guided tour — depart Reykjavik with a private driver-guide for the classic Golden Circle route. Begin at Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament was established. Walk the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting boiling water 20-30 meters into the air. Then visit the magnificent Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January with ice formations framing the cascading water. A truly spectacular winter scene.
day_by_day.evening: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — end the Golden Circle day with a soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and small geysers. The steam rising in the cold January air creates a magical, intimate atmosphere. Return to Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — fuel up for a full day of sightseeing
meals.lunch: Geysir Center restaurant or Friðheimar tomato farm restaurant (reservation required) — unique greenhouse dining surrounded by tomato plants, serving tomato-based menu items and house-made tomato schnapps
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik — celebrated restaurant in a historic fish factory, serving traditional Icelandic recipes with a modern twist; try the salted cod head or lamb neck

day_by_day.notes: A private Golden Circle tour (rather than group) allows flexibility in timing and stops. The Secret Lagoon is much more intimate than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic Icelandic hot spring experience. Book the Secret Lagoon in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir — experience one of the world's most unique dive sites. Silfra is the crack between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, filled with crystal-clear glacial water filtered through lava for decades (visibility up to 100 meters). Dry suit provided — water temperature is 2-4°C but you stay warm. An absolutely extraordinary premium adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik and visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass dome building offering a 360° panoramic viewing deck over Reykjavik and a remarkable 'Wonders of Iceland' exhibition featuring a real indoor ice cave, Northern Lights planetarium show, and geological displays.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Reykjavik evening — enjoy the city's cultural offerings. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for an evening performance (check schedule for classical or Icelandic folk music concerts). Followed by a premium farewell dinner at one of Reykjavik's top tables.

meals.breakfast: Sandholt Bakery, Reykjavik — Iceland's finest artisan bakery, serving exceptional pastries, sourdough breads, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Cozy post-dive warm-up lunch at Þingvellir Visitor Center café, or return to Reykjavik for lunch at Messinn — known for the best pan-fried fish in Iceland
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik — ultra-exclusive 12-seat counter dining experience with a surprise tasting menu; one of Iceland's most avant-garde culinary experiences (reservation essential months in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling/diving requires advance booking (e.g., DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures). Minimum age 12 for snorkeling, certification required for diving. Dry suit experience is not required. The water is shockingly clear — bring an underwater camera or rent a GoPro.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Reykjavik for the South Coast — private driver or rental car. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can walk behind the cascading curtain of water (may be icy in January — exercise caution). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, one of Iceland's most dramatic, with potential for ice crystal formations at the base in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Vík — Iceland's southernmost village. Explore the dramatic black sand beach of Reynisfjara, with its basalt column formations and powerful Atlantic waves (never turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are dangerous). Visit the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks rising from the surf.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at The Black Beach Suites or Hótel Kría near Vík — premium accommodation with views of the black sand coast and Mýrdalsjökull glacier. Settle in and enjoy the remote, dramatic atmosphere. Northern Lights vigil from the accommodation — the South Coast has excellent dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Luxury Reykjavik hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Skál! at Skógafoss — cozy café at the base of the waterfall serving hearty lamb soup and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — intimate restaurant serving Icelandic lamb, fresh fish, and local specialties with views of the black sand beach

day_by_day.notes: Drive carefully on the South Coast in January — ice and snow are common. Route 1 is generally maintained but can be slippery. Reynisfjara beach is genuinely dangerous — stay well back from the waterline and watch for sneaker waves. Book South Coast accommodation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull — drive east to Skaftafell within Vatnajökull National Park. Join a certified glacier guide for a premium small-group hike on Europe's largest glacier. Strap on crampons and explore stunning ice formations, blue ice caves, and crevasses. The January conditions create extraordinary blue ice colors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most iconic sights. Enormous blue-white icebergs calve from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drift through the lagoon before floating out to sea. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating a surreal icescape. Walk to Diamond Beach where ice blocks wash up on the black sand shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Vík or continue west to a midpoint accommodation. The drive back along the South Coast at dusk offers extraordinary winter light. Stop at Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon (if accessible) — a stunning 100-meter deep, 2km long canyon carved by glacial floods.

meals.breakfast: South Coast hotel breakfast — hearty Icelandic porridge and eggs to fuel the glacier hike
meals.lunch: Glacier Guides base camp café at Skaftafell — warm soup and sandwiches after the hike
meals.dinner: Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon restaurant (if staying nearby) or return dinner at Vík accommodation — Icelandic beef tenderloin with glacier lagoon views

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hike booking is essential — use a certified operator such as Glacier Guides or Arctic Adventures. All equipment (crampons, harness, helmet, ice axe) is provided. Dress in warm, waterproof layers. The blue ice caves inside Vatnajökull are an optional premium add-on (highly recommended — book separately).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning on the South Coast — revisit Skógafoss at sunrise (around 11:00 in January) for golden-hour photography of the waterfall. Walk the base of the falls and look for ice formations and frozen spray creating natural sculptures. Explore the Skógar Folk Museum — an open-air collection of traditional Icelandic turf houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula — visit the Bridge Between Continents (a footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver mud pools (Iceland's largest hot spring area with boiling mud and steam vents), and the dramatic coastal cliffs of Reykjanesviti lighthouse. Return to Reykjavik for final night.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Reykjavik — splurge on a premium farewell experience. Book a private Northern Lights boat tour from the Old Harbour — a small luxury vessel takes you out into Faxaflói Bay away from city lights for aurora viewing from the water, with champagne service on board.

meals.breakfast: South Coast hotel breakfast — final morning in the countryside
meals.lunch: Bryggjan Brugghús, Grindavík — a craft brewery and restaurant near the Reykjanes Peninsula serving excellent fish and chips and locally brewed beers
meals.dinner: Jómfrúin, Reykjavik — upscale Danish-Icelandic restaurant specializing in premium smørrebrød (open-faced sandwiches) with Icelandic toppings; intimate and elegant for a farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: The private Northern Lights boat tour is a truly unique and premium experience — book through Elding Whale Watching or Special Tours Reykjavik. Tours typically depart around 21:00-22:00 and last 2-3 hours. Champagne and warm blankets are usually provided.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik — enjoy a slow, luxurious breakfast at the hotel. Pack and check out. Spend remaining time browsing the Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets for last-minute premium Icelandic souvenirs: hand-knitted lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic design goods, local spirits (Brennivín, Icelandic gin), and artisan chocolates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Keflavík International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavik). Allow 3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse the Duty Free for Icelandic products. Relax in the airport's premium lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland — reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, glaciers, and Arctic nature. Icelandair flight home.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast — make it a celebration; order à la carte if available: eggs royale, smoked salmon platter, freshly squeezed juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Apotek Kitchen & Bar, Reykjavik (if time permits before transfer) — stylish restaurant in a historic pharmacy building serving elevated Icelandic comfort food
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal (Icelandair Saga Class offers elevated in-flight dining on international routes)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — traffic can be unpredictable. Keflavík Airport has good premium lounge facilities. Check Icelandair Saga Lounge access with your ticket class. Ensure all liquid purchases (spirits, skincare) comply with carry-on regulations or check them in. Iceland's Blue Lagoon Silica skin care products make excellent premium souvenirs.
